title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is a synthetic media incident in which a fabricated video was made to look like the output of a news organisation. The failure sits at the point of distribution rather than generation: a false claim was packaged with a real outlet's branding and pushed through a social platform account that presented as an ordinary user. The impersonation of the outlet is what gave the claim its apparent authority, and the platform's own enforcement only engaged on the trademark element after the outlet's lawyer complained.

Catching this kind of operation requires either platform-side detection of coordinated inauthentic accounts or verification by the outlet whose identity was borrowed. Neither is a check the individual viewer can perform. The view counts show the content circulated before any removal, so takedown was a response to reach, not a barrier to it.

The reporting attributes the network to Russian actors and describes the account as appearing to be a bot. That attribution is an assessment by the outlet and the tracking group, not a finding established in these facts. The claim about the payment is false on its face and no evidence for it is presented.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network known as Storm-1679 or Matryoshka has been spreading fake videos on US social media ahead of the 2026 midterms. One video, falsely branded with a Mother Jones logo, claimed the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. It was posted by an X account called роман, which appeared to be a bot, and drew 155,000 views within a day, plus 50,000 more from another account. The campaign has also used deepfakes of celebrities like Sarah Jessica Parker and Julia Roberts urging votes for Republicans.

After Mother Jones was alerted by the tracking group @antibot4navalny, its lawyer complained to X, which removed the post for a trademark violation. The operation has not yet gained major reach, but it echoes a 2024 campaign that pushed false anti-Democrat claims to millions. The article says the Trump administration has closed FBI, intelligence, and State Department units that once tracked Russian disinformation, leaving the US less able to counter such efforts.
